blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have progressed rapidly,
from neural radiance fields [ 25 ] to explicit Gaussian
primitives that render in real time [ 18 ] to surface aligned planar primitives like 2DGS [ 14 ] , and Triangle Splatting [ 13 ] .
These methods differ in geometry, but all face the same question: how much
of the scene can one primitive represent, and at what cost? This has led to the search for an overarching universal primitive which is efficient, expressive, and retains high geometric fidelity. This is even more important in resource-constrained settings, where efficiency includes not only rendering speed and model size but also the memory required during training.
Previous methods have often traded one aspect for another. For example, conventional Gaussian and triangle splats typically represent one view-conditioned color per primitive, so spatial variation emerges through many overlapping elements, leading to large overdraw . Others like BBSplat [ 33 ] add
per-primitive textures, or use shared neural appearance fields like NeST [ 39 ] and
Nexels [ 30 ] .
These methods increase per-element capacity, but move complexity into
textures, grids, or decoders. In contrast, we target the entire quality–efficiency trade-off at the primitive itself. For resource-constrained settings, this efficiency includes not only rendering
speed and model size, but also the memory required during training.

blocks.en: At constrained representation budgets, we seek a balance between geometric fidelity and appearance expressivity. Since agreement with training images alone does not guarantee accurate geometry [ 36 ] , we therefore target both surface reconstruction accuracy and novel-view rendering quality within a compact surface primitive.
blocks.zh: 在有限的代表性预算中,我们寻求在几何忠诚度和外观表达度之间取得平衡。 由于只同意训练图像并不能保证准确的几何[36],因此,我们的目标既包括表面重建的准确性,也包括在紧凑的表面原始范围内的新视觉渲染质量。

blocks.en: We are motivated by the idea that natural images and scenes are highly structured: large regions are often locally planar with smoothly varying appearance. An efficient surface primitive should therefore be able to exploit this underlying structure, wherever possible, and do so in a compact and self-contained manner.
blocks.zh: 我们的动机是,自然图像和场景结构严密:大区域往往是当地平原,外观平稳。 因此,一个高效的表面原始应能够尽可能利用这一基础结构,并以紧凑和自成一体的方式这样做。

a Hexel can represent such a region with one large primitive, including

blocks.en:
Why a hexagon? Regular hexagons tile a plane without gaps and cover more
area for the same boundary length than triangles or squares (other tileable primitives) [ 9 ] (discussed in Appendix G ).
When combined with the local color field, each Hexel can model both the region itself and smooth appearance variation within it.
In 3D, Hexels are rendered as oriented surface elements using
perspective-correct ray-plane intersection and depth-ordered blending.
The same primitive can be placed directly in the image plane for 2D image
representation. Thus, Hexels provide a single compact primitive family for
novel-view synthesis, surface reconstruction, and image representation,
without requiring texture maps, neural appearance fields, or decoding networks.

blocks.en: We evaluate Hexels for 3D novel view synthesis (memory-matched, primitive-matched, and unconstrained), surface reconstruction, and 2D image representation. We primarily use 34 scenes across DTU [ 16 ] , Tanks and Temples [ 21 ] , and Mip-NeRF360 [ 1 ] . At matched model sizes, Hexels improves PSNR over 2DGS by 4.53–7.38 dB with upto 3.6 × 3.6\times less VRAM requirements and over Triangle Splatting by 1.70–2.90 dB, with up to 1.87 × 1.87\times higher rendering FPS ( Table 2 ). At matched primitive budgets, Hexels improves PSNR over 2DGS by up to 4.74 dB, using 1.76 1.76 – 1.95 × 1.95\times less model size and upto 7 × 7\times less VRAM, and renders up to 2.31 × 2.31\times faster ( Table 3 ). Under unrestricted model sizes, Hexels still improve PSNR over 2DGS by 0.90 dB on both Tanks and Temples and DTU, while rendering 1.37 × 1.37\times and 2.26 × 2.26\times faster, respectively. For surface reconstruction, Hexels achieves 0.978 mm mean Chamfer distance over 15 DTU scans, versus 1.375 mm for 2DGS at the same model-memory budget (Table 5 ). On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, mean F1 for Hexels is 34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS (Table 6 ). Hexels also converges faster ( Figure 3 ) and improves 2D image representation over Image-GS [ 40 ] (Table 1 ).

blocks.en:
Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have improved rapidly since
NeRF [ 25 ] , which represents scenes as neural fields of
density and view-dependent radiance. Feature grids and explicit encodings
reduced their training and rendering cost [ 26 , 6 ] ,
while 3DGS [ 18 ] replaced neural fields with explicit
anisotropic Gaussian primitives, enabling real-time rasterization.
2DGS [ 14 ] further replaced volumetric Gaussians with planar
surfels, substantially improving surface reconstruction. These advances made
rendering faster and geometry more accurate, but efficient representation
requires more: high quality together with low model storage, low training
VRAM, few primitives, and high FPS. Appendix H discusses these trade-offs.

blocks.en:
Subsequent work improves different parts of this trade-off, but usually with
a catch. Triangle Splatting [ 13 ] , Deformable Beta
Splatting [ 23 ] , and 3D Convex Splatting [ 11 ] redesign the primitive or kernel to improve expressiveness or rendering
speed, but at cost of higher memory and VRAM usage. Hybrid methods such as
BBSplat [ 33 ] , NeST [ 39 ] , and
Nexels [ 30 ] reduce geometric redundancy by separating
geometry from appearance through textures or neural fields; this shifts
capacity into additional memory, training state, and computation. Other
methods retrofit existing representations through pruning, parameter
sharing, quantization, distillation, or baking [ 19 , 24 , 5 , 2 ] but still largely struggled to address the efficiency problem on all of its axes.
Hexels provides a solution to the efficiency problem by redesigning the primitive itself to exploit local structure and geometry in appearance.
The resulting primitive is compact in the form in which it is learned and
rendered, simultaneously targeting storage, training VRAM, primitive count,
FPS, and reconstruction quality. Further, unlike previous works, Hexels are general surface
primitives: the same underlying design applies directly to oriented 3D
surfaces and to 2D images without major changes to the representation or
optimization.

blocks.en: 3 Hexels: Hexagonal Surface Elements
blocks.zh: 3 螺旋:六边形表面元素

blocks.en:
We introduce Hexels , planar hexagonal surface elements designed to reduce overlap and overdraw, avoid the long tails of Gaussian footprints, and represent more appearance within each primitive. Each Hexel combines a soft hexagonal support with a first-order spatial color field, allowing a single primitive to cover a larger coherent surface region while modeling smooth appearance variation within it. In 3D, a Hexel is an oriented planar patch with a local 2D coordinate
system. Following 2DGS [ 14 ] , we evaluate each primitive at the perspective-correct ray-plane intersection and blend the resulting contributions in depth order.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍Hexels, 六边形表面元素 旨在减少重叠和过度拉伸 避免高斯足迹的长尾巴, 并代表每个原始体中更多的外观。 每个Hexel将软六边形支持与一阶空间色域相结合,允许单个原始物覆盖更大的连贯的表面区域,同时模拟其中的平滑外观变化. 在 3D 中,一个 Hexel 是一个带有本地 2D 坐标的面向平面板块
系统。 在2DGS[14]之后,我们评价每个原始的光线-平面交叉点,并按深度顺序混合由此产生的贡献。

blocks.en:
Like BBSplat’s fixed-storage comparisons [ 33 ] , we constrain baseline primitive counts and other learned components to compare methods under matched uncompressed model-memory budgets.
Table 2 compares all methods at the V1 model-memory
budget along with corresponding training resources and rendering rates; additional comparisons at the V2 and V3 budgets are provided in Appendix I.1 . At matched model-memory budgets, Hexels V1 improves PSNR over 2DGS
by 4.53–7.38 dB and over Triangle Splatting by 1.70–2.90 dB across the
three benchmarks. Average rendering speed (FPS) range from 377.8 to 830.8 FPS, or 1.54 1.54 – 1.87 × 1.87\times those of 2DGS. On Mip-NeRF360, the mean PSNR gain is 6.99 dB. All these improvements come with upto 3.6 × 3.6\times less VRAM usage than 2DGS.
Figure 4 shows that Hexels retain fine scene structure
under these compact memory budgets. This matched-memory evaluation is our
primary efficiency setting, in which Hexels establish the strongest overall
quality–efficiency trade-off among the evaluated methods. Full experimental
details are provided in Appendix E.1 .

blocks.en: We further evaluate surface reconstruction on all 15 DTU scans and 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes. As can be seen from the results (Table 5 ), our primary comparison is with 2DGS, and our primary setting is memory-matched and primitive-matched as before, while we also report unconstrained results. Table 5 reports mean DTU Chamfer distance (CD). Hexels reaches 0.978 mm, compared with 1.375 mm and 1.449 mm for the memory- and primitive-controlled 2DGS variants. blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced Hexels, a general surface primitive, for 2D and 3D, that exploits the local structure of the data it represents: hexagonal support efficiently covers
coherent surface regions, while a first-order spatial color field models
appearance variation within each primitive. Across our three 3D benchmarks,
Hexels establish a new quality–efficiency frontier among the evaluated surface-aligned representations, improving PSNR by up to 7.38 dB at
matched model memory, using lower peak training VRAM and
up to 2 × \times less learned state at matched primitive count, while rendering up
to 2.31 × \times faster than 2DGS. The same primitive also performs strongly
for memory-constrained surface reconstruction and directly generalizes to
efficient 2D image representation. Hexels therefore move efficiency into the
primitive itself, opening a path toward high-quality novel-view synthesis
and explicit surface reconstruction on edge and resource-constrained
hardware.

blocks.en:
A first-order color model cannot represent arbitrary texture within a
single primitive. High-frequency or uncorrelated appearance requires
smaller primitives or a richer color model, reducing the expected benefit
of exploiting local smoothness. Sparse initialization can also leave parts of a scene
poorly covered, and the independent surface cells do not form a watertight
mesh. Sharper footprints do not by themselves prevent sampling artifacts,
especially at small projected sizes or grazing views.
Hexels does not outperform every baseline on every metric;
the appendix provides the full comparisons. Our current primitives are planar. A natural extension is developable Hexels: curved patches with zero Gaussian curvature that remain locally isometric to the planar canonical hexagon. Such primitives could bend along one principal direction, for example, as cylindrical or conical patches, while preserving the simple 2D footprint and affine appearance parameterization. This may allow individual primitives to cover larger regions of locally near-developable geometry without introducing additional overlap.

blocks.zh: 附录C

blocks.en: Hexels (V1/V2/V3 - Fixed) do not primarily use densification and pruning to avoid exceeding memory and/or primitive constraints in our primary experiments. Given our focus on practical efficiency, we want to avoid any hacks to improve our performance by temporarily going over the memory or primitive limits - which is why the peak VRAM values are very important, as often, other efficiency-focused methods do not report them. We, however, also report the densified NVS and surface reconstruction counterparts in our results - primarily in unconstrained settings - which are not the focus of our work. Notably, our baseline methods are allowed to temporarily exceed memory and primitive constraints to achieve better results, as they often perform much worse when forced to remain below these requirements.
blocks.zh: Hexels(V1/V2/V3 - 固定)主要不使用密度和挤压来避免我们初级实验中的超载内存和/或原始约束. 鉴于我们注重实际效率,我们希望避免任何通过暂时超越内存或原始限制来改善我们业绩的黑客入侵,这就是为什么高峰的VRAM值非常重要,就像其他注重效率的方法常常不报告它们一样. 然而,我们还报告说,我们的成果中,主要是在不受限制的环境中,有变质的NVS和地面重建对应方,这些不是我们工作的重点。 值得注意的是,允许我们的基线方法暂时超过记忆和原始限制,以取得更好的结果,因为当它们被迫保持在这些要求以下时,其表现往往更糟。

blocks.en: Our densification strategy is similar to 3DGS and 2DGS. Between two growth triggers, for each Hexel, we track the norm of the loss gradient with respect to its projected 2D center, averaged over the iterations in which the Hexel is visible. A Hexel becomes a parent Hexel when this average is large, it was visible often enough, and it is not too young. Small parents are cloned, and large parents are split. A parent Hexel counts as small when its larger tangent scale is at most 1% of the scene extent. A clone is a copy of the parent Hexel whose center is moved within the parent’s tangent plane by a random Gaussian offset, scaled by the parent’s two scales. A split replaces the parent with two children, each offset randomly in the same plane, with both scales divided by 1.6 1.6 , as in 3DGS, and an opacity o child = 1 − 1 − o parent o_{\mathrm{child}}=1-\sqrt{1-o_{\mathrm{parent}}} . New Hexels copy the parent’s appearance coefficients.

blocks.en: A Hexel can be used to specify a hexagonal cell through d ⁡ ( u , v ) = 0 d(u,v)=0 in Eq. ( 2 ). The six vertices can be mapped analytically into the world space through Eq. ( 1 ). Importantly, this is differentiable and can be done in constant time per Hexel or any other polygonal primitive with low overdraw. However, this might not be possible for the more prevalent Gaussian-based surfels like 2DGS. A Gaussian surfel [ 14 ] has a smooth local representation G ( u , v ) = exp [ − ( u 2 + v 2 ) / 2 ] G(u,v)=\exp[-(u^{2}+v^{2})/2] , with no explicitly finite boundary; therefore, getting such a differentiable, constant-time surface cell representation is non-trivial.

A Gaussian surfel [14] 具有平滑的局部代表G(u, v) = exp [−(u 2 + v 2) / 2] G(u,v) exp [-(u^{2}+v^{2})/2],没有明确限定的边界;因此,获得这样不同的,恒定的表面细胞代表是非三角的.

blocks.en: Table 8 (a) reports 1.575 mm CD without either loss, 1.246 mm with depth distortion alone, 0.986 mm with normal consistency alone and 0.978 mm with both losses. Normal consistency provides the larger individual improvement, with a smaller complementary benefit from depth distortion.

blocks.zh: 附录G 为什么是六边形和空间颜色?

blocks.en:
We want each Hexel to represent a large surface region without losing the
appearance variation inside it. This requires two choices: a shape that
can cover surfaces efficiently, and a color model that can describe more
than a constant color. The honeycomb theorem motivates the first choice:
regular hexagons minimize boundary length among equal-area partitions of
the plane [ 9 ] . The spatial color field addresses
the second.

blocks.en: Appendix H Extended Related Work
blocks.zh: 附录H 扩大的相关工作

blocks.en:
NeRF [ 25 ] was introduced for novel view synthesis and
represents a scene as a neural field of density and view-dependent radiance.
This representation enabled high-quality novel-view rendering. However, the
repeated network evaluations required for volumetric rendering made the
original NeRF expensive to train and slow to render. A large body of
follow-up work introduced explicit feature grids, hash encodings,
precomputed representations, and baked representations to reduce the
sampling, rendering, and computational demands of the original neural-field
models [ 26 , 6 , 28 ] .
blocks.zh:
NERF [25] 被引入用于新颖的视图综合和
代表作为密度和视线依赖光度的神经场景.
这一表述使得能够进行高质量的小说视觉渲染。 然而,
进行量子渲染所需的重复网络评价
原始的 NERF 昂贵的训练 和缓慢的制作。 一大块
后续工作引入了明确的特征网格,散列编码,
预编的表述,以及制作的表述,以减少
原始神经场的取样、渲染和计算需求
型号 [26, 6, 28].

blocks.en:
3DGS [ 18 ] introduced an alternative for substantially
more efficient rendering using explicit anisotropic Gaussian volume
primitives, enabling real-time rasterization. However, because of their
volumetric nature, 3D Gaussians are not naturally surface aligned and can
produce inaccurate geometry. To remedy this, works such as
SuGaR [ 7 ] regularize Gaussians toward surfaces. An
important solution was introduced by 2DGS [ 14 ] , which
instead represents the scene using oriented planar Gaussian surfels and
perspective-correct ray–plane intersections, retaining fast rasterization
while substantially improving the geometry.

3DGS [18] 引入了一种实质性
使用显式异同位素高斯体积进行更有效的渲染
原始的,可以实时光栅化. 然而,由于

代之以面向高斯海面的浮雕和
视角正确射线-平面交叉点,保留快速光栅化
同时大大改进了几何学。

blocks.en:
Despite the large improvements made by 3DGS and 2DGS in training and
rendering time relative to NeRF, these improvements are still not enough for
truly resource-constrained settings. Efficiency requires several things at
the same time: learned model storage and training VRAM should be as low as
possible, primitive count should remain small relative to the cost of each
primitive, and the representation should still retain high reconstruction
quality and fast rendering. 3DGS and 2DGS can both require large primitive
populations and substantial memory. Despite this, we find that 2DGS remains
the strongest prior native surface representation in terms of the overall
performance–efficiency balance when these factors are considered together,
even after a number of subsequent works have attempted to improve different
parts of the problem.

相对于NERF,这些改进仍然不足以
真正受资源限制的设置。 效率需要很多东西

从总体来看,以前最强的原生地表代表性

即使后来的一些作品试图改进不同的
问题的一部分。

blocks.en:
Different follow-up works have tried to make the primitive more expressive,
reduce the number of primitives, increase rendering speed, reduce model
storage, or address limitations of 2DGS and earlier Gaussian
representations, such as the infinite support of Gaussian kernels.
GES [ 10 ] , for example, replaces the Gaussian with a more
flexible generalized exponential kernel, while Deformable Beta
Splatting [ 23 ] introduces bounded and deformable kernels.
3D Convex Splatting [ 11 ] instead uses smooth 3D convex
primitives, allowing more flexible volumetric geometry and sharper
boundaries, but remains a volumetric rather than surface-aligned
representation.

减少原始数量, 增加渲染速度, 减少模型

blocks.en:
Triangle Splatting [ 13 ] , on the other hand, optimizes an
independent triangle soup so that high rendering speeds can be achieved while
retaining a surface-aligned primitive. However, high-quality scenes can still
require very large triangle populations, increasing both model storage and
the computation and memory required during optimization. The independent
triangle soup also does not provide surface connectivity.
MeshSplatting [ 12 ] follows this work by introducing explicit
connectivity and an opaque mesh representation, trading the independence of
individual splats for a conventional connected surface. Other works increase
geometric complexity in different ways, including Quadratic Gaussian
Splatting [ 41 ] , which introduces curved patches, and
MILo [ 8 ] , which brings mesh construction directly into
Gaussian optimization. In our experiments, we focus on 2DGS, Triangle Splatting, and MeshSplatting, which we find provide the strongest overall quality–efficiency trade-offs among prior native surface-aligned representations.

blocks.en:
Hexels are also primitive-based renderers, but we try to solve a more
fundamental problem: can we design a more efficient primitive that is able
to exploit the structure found in the world, both in geometry and
appearance? Like 2DGS, we retain independent planar elements, but change the
region represented by one element and the signal represented inside it. We
use an affine hexagonal patch, which gives a large, nearly isotropic local
region, together with a first-order color field that models smooth
appearance variation across a surface. We find that much of the variation
on local surfaces is smooth, making such a representation particularly
efficient.

blocks.en:
A first-order color field, by itself, is not unique to Hexels: a vertex-colored
triangle (another tiling primitive), for example, can also represent an affine color field. The domain
of our primitive, however, makes an important difference. Under the same
local approximation-error ellipse, our analysis shows that the largest
admissible affine regular hexagon can cover twice the area of the
corresponding affine triangle and about 1.3 × 1.3\times that of the square
(Appendix G ). Hexels therefore increase the
amount represented by a simple planar element without requiring complex
geometry, volumetric convexes, or mesh connectivity.

blocks.en:
The most direct comparisons to Hexels are fundamentally native surface
primitives. However, there has also been a trend toward hybrid
representations that separate geometry from appearance in order to improve
particular aspects of efficiency over 2DGS-like representations.
Gaussian Billboards [ 35 ] , for example, introduces
spatially varying appearance through per-splat texture interpolation.
BBSplat [ 33 ] learns separate RGB and alpha texture maps
to reduce the number of geometric primitives required. This can substantially
reduce primitive count, but the textures themselves become part of the model
and training cost.
NeST [ 39 ] follows a related idea by separating sparse surface
geometry from a neural appearance representation. Nexels [ 30 ] similarly combines sparse surfels with a shared neural
appearance field and per-primitive colors. These methods can substantially
reduce geometric primitive count, but this capacity is moved into texture
maps, feature fields, or neural networks, which introduce additional memory,
training state, and computation.
Concurrent work such as Bake It Till You Make
It [ 17 ] , which is also centered on improving the efficiency
of surface splats, follows this hybrid direction. It uses sparse surface
geometry together with a hash-based appearance representation during
optimization, and later bakes high-frequency appearance into a texture atlas
for rendering. This can reduce the number of geometric surface primitives
and improve rendering speed, but appearance is again moved outside the
primitive and requires a separate representation and baking pipeline.

blocks.en:
These ideas of separating geometry and appearance, neural textures, and
texture baking are interesting, but they can in principle be applied on top of
different native surface primitives. They also often come with a different set of trade-offs, be it slower rendering, more memory or non-ideal decoupled optimization. They therefore answer a somewhat
different question from ours. We include these methods in our comparisons,
but count their full learned representation, including textures, feature
grids, and neural decoders, rather than only the number of geometric
elements. These hybrid setups, however, are not the objective of our work.

纹理烘焙很有趣 但原则上可以应用在
不同的原生表层原始。 它们也常常有一套不同的取舍,无论是较慢的渲染,更多的内存还是非理想的脱钩优化. 因此他们回答一个问题

但数一下他们完全学会的表现,包括纹理,特征
网格和神经解码器,而不仅仅是几何数
要素。 然而,这些混合结构不是我们工作的目标。

blocks.en:
Given the multifaceted nature of the efficiency problem, another body of work
has developed around interventions on existing primitives to improve
different aspects of their efficiency. Scaffold-GS [ 24 ] ,
for example, reduces 3DGS redundancy through anchors that generate
view-adaptive Gaussian attributes rather than storing every Gaussian
independently. 3DGS-MCMC [ 19 ] improves primitive
allocation through stochastic updates and relocation. FastGS [ 29 ] instead focuses on training time, using
multi-view-consistent densification and pruning to reduce unnecessary
Gaussian growth.
blocks.zh:

围绕现有原始物的干预措施,发展了改进
其效率的不同方面。 脚手架-GS [24],
例如,通过生成的锚减少3DGS冗余

多视图一致的密度和冲动以减少不必要的
高斯生长.

blocks.en:
A related line of work compresses already learned representations.
LightGaussian [ 5 ] prunes low-importance Gaussians,
distills appearance into lower-order spherical harmonics, and applies vector
quantization to reduce model size. Compact 3D Gaussian
Representation [ 22 ] combines learnable masking with
shared neural appearance, vector quantization, and entropy coding.
Compressed 3DGS [ 27 ] similarly uses
quantization-aware clustering and codebooks to reduce storage. Related ideas
have also been developed for surface-based Gaussian representations.

blocks.en:
These methods are useful and complementary, but they start with an already
chosen primitive and add additional methodology around it. They may greatly
improve one aspect of efficiency without necessarily reducing the memory and
computation required elsewhere, particularly during training. Our focus is
therefore the more fundamental question: we can add pruning, quantization,
codebooks, texture atlases, neural decoders, and other post-hoc compression,
but can we also start with a more efficient native surface primitive?
Hexels address this question before these additional techniques are applied;
many of them could still be applied on top of Hexels afterward.

这些方法是有用和互补的,但从已经

但能否从更高效的原始地表开始?
在应用这些额外技术之前,Hexels先处理这一问题;
其中许多仍然可以应用在Hexels之上。

blocks.en:
A similar line of research has developed independently in 2D, where neural
image representations are used to encode visual media. Earlier approaches
often relied on autoencoders or implicit neural functions. More recently,
GaussianImage [ 38 ] adapted ideas from Gaussian
splatting to represent images using simple 2D Gaussian primitives,
demonstrating fast fitting and rendering. Image-GS [ 40 ] further improves this representation using content-adaptive initialization
and progressive optimization of anisotropic 2D Gaussians.
SAD [ 15 ] instead represents the image through a soft
anisotropic partition whose regions depend on neighboring sites rather than
independently parameterized primitives. We compare Hexels primarily with Image-GS because both use independently parameterized image primitives, enabling a direct comparison of quality and efficiency per primitive. SAD instead represents images through a coupled partition whose regions depend on neighboring sites, addressing a different representation regime that we leave for future comparison.

显示快速的适应和渲染。 Image-GS [40] 利用内容适应初始化进一步改善这种表述方式
并逐渐优化异构2D高斯人.
SAD [15] 通过软体代表图像
区域依赖邻近地点而不是
独立参数化原始。 我们主要比较Hexels和Image-GS,因为两者都使用独立参数化的图像原始物,使得每个原始物能够直接比较质量和效率. 相反,SAD通过一个组合的分区代表图像,这些分区的地区依赖于邻近的场址,涉及不同的代表制度,我们留待今后进行比较。

blocks.en:
We show that Hexels can also be used directly for 2D image representation,
where they outperform Image-GS in reconstruction quality and training
convergence under our evaluated settings. More importantly, Hexels are
designed as a general surface primitive rather than separate 2D and 3D
representations. In 2D, the primitive is placed directly in the image plane;
in 3D, it is oriented on a surface patch. While the compositor changes where
required by visibility and depth ordering, the basic hexagonal support and
appearance model remain the same. This gives Hexels a general capability
across image representation, novel-view synthesis, and surface
reconstruction, rather than requiring a separate representation for each
setting.

我们显示Hexels也可以直接用于2D图像表示,
他们表现优于 重建质量和培训中的图像-GS
在我们评价的环境下,趋同。 更重要的是,赫克塞尔是
设计为一般表面原始,而不是单独的2D和3D
说明。 在2D中,原始物直接放置在图像平面中;
在3D中,它面向一个表面补丁. 当混凝土改变在哪里
根据可见度和深度顺序、基本六边形支持和
外观模式不变。 这让Hexels拥有一般能力
跨图像表现、小说-视觉合成和表面
重建,而不是要求每个组织单独派驻代表
设置。

blocks.en:
A common pattern across methods that have tried to make surface-aligned
representations more efficient is that the cost is often moved to another
part of the problem. Faster rasterization may still require a very large
primitive population. Sparse geometry may move capacity into external
texture maps or neural fields, increasing representation complexity,
training VRAM, or final model storage. Compression can make the deployed
scene small while having much less effect on the size and memory required
during training. Richer geometry can reduce primitive count while increasing
the cost of each primitive.
blocks.zh:
试图使表面对齐的各种方法的共同模式
更有效率的表示是,费用往往转移到另一个
问题的一部分。 更快的光栅化可能还需要很大
原始人口. Sparse 几何可以将容量移到外部
纹理图或神经领域, 越来越复杂,
训练VRAM,或最终型号存储. 压缩可以使部署
场景较小,但对所需大小和内存的影响要小得多
训练期间。 丰富的几何可以减少原始数,同时增加
每个原始人的成本。

blocks.en:
Hexels are designed to alleviate these problems together, without first
resorting to post-hoc retrofitting and before pruning or compression is
applied. We use the fact that natural images, surfaces, and scenes contain
local structure. Large regions are often approximately planar and vary
smoothly in appearance. A Hexel covers a bounded, efficient local region and
models first-order appearance variation inside it, allowing simple regions
to be represented by larger and fewer elements. This allows us to target high
quality, low learned storage, low training VRAM, few primitives, and high
FPS in the same native surface representation, in both 2D and 3D. Pruning,
quantization, neural appearance models, and other post-hoc improvements
remain possible additions rather than requirements of the representation.
blocks.zh:
螺旋桨旨在共同缓解这些问题,不首先
使用热处理后改造,在压缩或压缩之前

地方结构。 大片地区往往大致是平原,而且各不相同

由更大和更少的元素代表。 这样我们就能瞄准高点
质量、学习程度低的存储器、培训程度低的VRAM、少数原始人和高
FPS在同一原生地表代表物中,在2D和3D中都有. 普鲁宁
量化、神经外观模型和其他热后改进
仍然是可能增加的,而不是代表的要求。

blocks.en: I.3 Deployment Compression analysis
blocks.zh: I.3 部署压缩分析

blocks.en:
While outside our core efficiency objectives, we also provide an initial analysis of lossless compression and appearance parameter quantization
(PQ1024) on all six variants across 34 scenes.
Our lossless compression analysis keeps every FP32 parameter
exact. It regroups the bytes of each parameter array by position (all first
bytes of the 4-byte values, then all second bytes, and so on), so that the
highly repetitive sign and exponent bytes are stored together. It then
compresses the result with DEFLATE [ 4 ] , the standard
LZ77 and Huffman-coding compressor used by ZIP and gzip software.
PQ1024 replaces RGB appearance vectors with 1,024-entry codebooks:
one per SH coefficient for V3, and corresponding codebooks for the
spatial and directional gradients of V1/V2.
Geometry and base color remain lossless.
Parameters are decoded to FP32 before rendering, without retraining.
